cancelStream(uint256).notice: Stop the stream: installments not yet vested refund to the payer         immediately; vested-but-unclaimed installments stay claimable.

claimInstallment(uint256).notice: Claim every vested-but-unclaimed installment. Works after         cancellation too: installments vested by cancellation stay the         payee's.

createStream(address,uint256,uint256,uin.notice: Pre-fund a payroll stream: the full amount for all periods is         pulled up front. One installment vests per elapsed period.

raiseDispute(uint256).notice: Either party freezes the escrow into dispute. All automatic         settlement paths stop applying; the public jury decides.

resolveDispute(uint256).notice: Settle a dispute after the jury window closes. Anyone may call.         Majority wins the full amount; a tie (including no votes at         all) splits 50/50 with rounding dust to the payer.

submitEvidence(uint256,string).notice: A party publishes evidence for the jury (an IPFS/URL link to         their materials) while voting is open.

vote(uint256,bool).notice: Vote in an open dispute. One vote per address; the two parties         cannot vote. `supportPayee` = the payee should be paid in full,         otherwise the payer should be refunded in full.

documentation.text:
@title MilePayV2 — milestone escrow with public-jury dispute resolution and payroll streams
 @notice Extends the MilePay v1 escrow (built in Arc Studio, deployed on Arc Mainnet)
         with two new primitives:
         1. Public jury arbitration: if either party disputes before settlement, the
            escrow freezes and both sides publish evidence. Anyone else may vote
            during the jury window; the majority decides who is paid. A tie splits
            the amount 50/50. No single arbiter exists to bribe, coerce, or trust.
         2. Payroll streams: a payer pre-funds N periods of salary; one installment
            vests per period and the payee claims vested installments at any time.
         The v1 guarantees are unchanged: the payer can never redirect escrowed
         funds, and every settlement path is enforced by the contract alone.
